text: What did Gödel's 1949 solution to Einstein's field equations demonstrate about the topology of time?
choices: That closed timelike curves — trajectories always locally future-directed yet globally looping back to their own starting event — are consistent with general relativity, making temporal topology a contingent physical matter
That the laws of physics actively prevent the formation of any time loops through quantum gravitational effects
That time must be discrete at the Planck scale, with spacetime emerging from an underlying causal set
That the universe had a smooth, boundaryless origin when described in imaginary time
explanation: Gödel's rotating-universe solution contains closed timelike curves, showing that CTCs are compatible with Einstein's equations and that temporal topology is physically contingent rather than fixed by logic. Option 1 states Hawking's rival Chronology Protection Conjecture, option 2 is the causal set program, and option 3 is the Hartle-Hawking no-boundary proposal — all distinct claims from this unit.
